text:
Maya (marketing): Hey team — final copy for the launch post references 2x lower per-token cost and ~20% lower p95 latency vs baseline. Can runtime help validate those claims with a quick reproducible data pack we can attach to the PR? We need: model variants (fp16, int8/quantized), 1k sample payloads, per-token latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99), cold-start vs warmed, and the exact commit used. Deadline EOD Tue. :pray:

Sam (eng/runtime): Can do. Quick Qs — which model and exact baseline are we comparing to? Also want to confirm target seq lengths and concurrency and whether streaming was used in the claim.

Maya (marketing): Model is redwood-13b-v1 (the hosted perf profile). Baseline is public-x-model-13b (what we used in the benchmark doc). Use 128/512/2k sequence length buckets. For concurrency mimic light web traffic: 10 rps steady, 1 rps burst. Streaming off for latency numbers.

Priya (eng-runtime): Got it. We'll run three variants: fp16, int8-fast, int8-safe (different quant profiles). We'll produce CSVs with per-request token breakdown and a summarized JSON with percentiles. Will need the sample prompts set — do you have that?

Maya (marketing): I'll upload a sanitized payload pack to the marketing drive in a minute. It includes 1k examples split by length bucket. Also include a smaller eval set (200) for quality check against the baseline.

Alex (eng-ml): Heads up: quantized int8-safe may shift LM score a bit on the eval set. If you want claim-level parity, please specify allowed delta (e.g., <= 1% BLEU-like / model score). Otherwise we should call out quality delta.

Tony (marketing): For messaging, we can tolerate up to 2% quality delta as long as cost/latency gains are clear. If delta >2% call it out and we'll adjust wording.

Sam (eng/runtime): Thanks. Plan: 1) smoke run on staging to verify harness and env; 2) full sweep (3 variants x 3 seq buckets x warm/cold) 3) export: raw CSV per-run + summary table + artifacts (traces, flame graphs for the hotspot). We'll pin the runtime commit and container hash and attach the perf job link.

runtime-bot: perf-job queued -> https://ci.redwood/internal/jobs/87654 :clock1:  (expected runtime ~45m)

Priya (eng-runtime): Running smoke now. Command we’ll use (for reproducibility):

```
python infra/perf/harness.py \
  --model redwood-13b-v1 \
  --variant int8-fast \
  --input gs://marketing/launch_payloads/1k.jsonl \
  --seq-buckets 128,512,2048 \
  --concurrency 10 \
  --burst 1 \
  --streaming false \
  --output gs://perf-artifacts/launch-2026-03-XX/
```

Priya (eng-runtime): Also logging: gpu_type, host_cpu, per-token-latency-ms, total-req-latency-ms, tokens-emitted, kv-cache-hits. We'll include raw per-token traces for a random 50 requests per bucket.

Maya (marketing): Awesome. Please flag any instability or high variance. If p95 is > 20% different from earlier numbers, pause and ping me. Need the summary table + raw CSVs for the press kit.

Sam (eng/runtime): Understood. We'll upload artifacts to the same GS path and ping when done. If the smoke fails we'll open a thread in #eng-runtime and tag you. :thumbsup:

Tony (marketing): One more ask — can you include a short reproducibility README with the exact docker image and a single command to re-run the full sweep? Reviewers might want to run locally.

Priya (eng-runtime): Yup. We'll include a README.md with docker pull, env vars, and the harness command. Also note: quantization RNG is seeded; we'll record seeds in the summary.

Maya (marketing): Thank you!! If we get green, we'll include a small table and link to the artifact in the blog. :eyes:

runtime-bot: perf-job completed -> https://ci.redwood/internal/jobs/87654 (artifacts: gs://perf-artifacts/launch-2026-03-XX)

Sam (eng/runtime): Upload complete. Artifacts: summary.json, runs/*.csv, traces/*.jsonl, README.md. p95 numbers match claim within 8% for int8-fast and 18% for int8-safe vs baseline; int8-safe shows a 1.8% eval delta on the eval set.

Maya (marketing): Great — will craft the wording to mention the safe quantization tradeoff. Can you paste the exact summary table here?

Sam (eng/runtime): Pasted summary (short):
- fp16: cost baseline 1.0x, p95 120ms
- int8-fast: cost 0.55x, p95 110ms
- int8-safe: cost 0.48x, p95 98ms (eval delta 1.8%)

Alex (eng-ml): Looks reasonable. Recommend a brief note in the blog about eval set and allowed delta.

Maya (marketing): Perfect. Thank you all. I'll wait for the README link and then finalize copy. :rocket:
